verdict: F02 IS AN ENVIRONMENT EFFECT, NOT A REGRESSION
why: the identical discovery argv fails with EXACTLY the same 8 failures + 2 errors when run against the PRE-REPAIR base commit exported as an archive, so the failure profile predates this round and is not introduced by it

the failing modules are the ones that require git history or build outputs (test_publication_projection needs a local frozen ref; test_wheel_distribution needs built artifacts; test_evidence_manifest / test_tooling_executes / test_atomic_requirements need a real checkout and tracked-file metadata)
in a proper checkout the base passes 325/325 and the candidate passes 383/383, i.e. this round adds 58 tests and introduces zero new failures
the independent checker deliberately did NOT run the suite in the candidate cwd (its own read-only rule), so it could only observe the archive/clone environment, which cannot pass those modules
residual_risk_stated_plainly: the operator's PASS above and the checker's FAIL are both correct statements about different environments. Neither is a claim of upstream semantic correctness.
action: no repair required for F02; the environment dependency of 10 test modules is disclosed as a Known Limitation and handed to TT as a harness-hardening item (make the suite archive-safe or mark those modules environment-gated).
